summary: C1: schema + tier limits + FALLBACK_PRICING refresh
description:
Data-layer changes the rest of the work depends on. BRD §6.1, §6.2, §6.4.

Files:
  - migrations/009_user_model_pref.sql (new) — single ALTER TABLE
    user_preferences ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS preferred_model TEXT.
    Nullable. Null = 'use tier default.'
  - src/lib/spend.ts — TIER_LIMITS const update only:
      free  → { query_limit: 10,  usd_limit: null }   (unchanged)
      pro   → { query_limit: 100, usd_limit: 5.00  }   (was { 30, null })
  - scripts/sync-pricing.ts — FALLBACK_PRICING gains the four
    picker IDs (deepseek-v4-pro, x-ai/grok-4.3,
    anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, openai/gpt-5.4) plus keeps
    deepseek-chat for one release as a safety net.
  - src/__tests__/spend.test.ts (extend) — assert dual-axis on pro:
    usd cap binds at $5 even when queries-cap hasn't.

Done when:
  - Migration applies cleanly under deploy.sh's
    'psql -1 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1' (re-running is the test).
  - npx tsc --noEmit clean.
  - reserveBudget({ tier: 'pro', estimatedCostUsd: 5.01 }) returns
    { allowed: false, reason: 'usd' } with queries_used = 0.
  - Existing pro-budget tests still pass with the new caps.

Tests: vitest (unit). No DB integration test needed — IF NOT EXISTS
DDL + the existing reserveBudget unit tests cover it.

Operator action post-merge: migration auto-applies on next deploy.
TIER_LIMITS rewrite kicks in on the next reserveBudget UPSERT for
each user, atomically. No env or config change needed.

Blocks: all subsequent tickets — C2's resolver wires into a route
that reads from this column; C3 needs the $5 cap; C4 tests
require both.
